label: Demand intensity is real (8.3 per-mention, most enthusiastic open-text)
kill_criterion: Independent quant (n=39 and larger) shows the enthusiasm was an artifact of the shared 8-person qual base, not a durable signal.
test_that_resolves_it: Cross-check intensity against the independent survey cut and any n=119 open-text; separate category-enthusiasm from feature-switch intent.
evidence: [R/D] CS:HIGH on enthusiasm - 8.3 n=8 + most enthusiastic open-text. But n=8 shares the qual base with the #3 qual rank (H8); only n=39 adds independence.

label: Diagnostic delta beats Rost/Thread/PIA/incumbents (THE CORE BET)
kill_criterion: On real anonymized tickets, ACP's diagnosis is not measurably better than Rost/Thread/PIA or a PSA-native classifier - no wedge, only a commodity router.
test_that_resolves_it: Blind bench-test ACP diagnosis vs Rost/Thread/PIA on a corpus of real anonymized tickets; measure accuracy and time-to-context delta with MSP judges.
evidence: [A - untested, Beth-tagged core bet]. CS:LOW. Compounded by the fact the diagnostic capability is not in the day-1 build (FSN-82692).

label: The wedge is live diagnostics, not classification (classification = table stakes)
kill_criterion: Buyers value the classification/routing enough on its own that diagnostics are not needed to differentiate - OR classification turns out NOT to be table stakes.
test_that_resolves_it: Kano survey on classification vs diagnostics; confirm classification lands as must-be and diagnostics as performance/delighter.
evidence: [R] CS:HIGH that classification is table-stakes (offerings labels it table-stakes-in-PSA; #6 forced-rank). The framing is sound; the risk is that the wedge half is unbuilt.

label: Superpower holds: SOC pattern data + PSA integration depth power the diagnosis
kill_criterion: The SOC auto-remediation corpus does not generalize to PSA ticket diagnosis, or PSA integration depth is shallower than the pitch (see H5 single-PSA).
test_that_resolves_it: Map SOC corpus categories to the actual ticket taxonomy; confirm coverage; audit PSA integration depth beyond ConnectWise.
evidence: [A]/[R]. CS:MEDIUM. SOC corpus is a real superpower for A; its transfer to ticket-level diagnosis is assumed, not demonstrated.

label: Safe-auto vs human-sign-off line matches where MSPs expect it (MSP-C separation-of-duties)
kill_criterion: MSPs want the auto/approve line drawn differently (more human sign-off, or different risk tiers), so the day-1 auto-execute either scares them or feels useless.
test_that_resolves_it: Operator interviews (5-8 MSPs) on which triage/dispatch actions they'd allow auto vs require sign-off day-1.
evidence: [A] CS:LOW - single MSP-C anchor for separation-of-duties. Auto/batch line is spec'd (FSN-82692) but not validated against buyer expectation.

label: Commodity risk is survivable (RMM/PSA won't fold triage in first)
kill_criterion: ConnectWise/Autotask/Halo or the RMM ships native triage/classification free, commoditizing D before it monetizes.
test_that_resolves_it: Track incumbent roadmaps; test whether the diagnostic delta (D2) is enough to survive a free native classifier.
evidence: [R] CS:HIGH that the objection is real - 'it'll be built into my RMM/PSA' recurred >=4/5. Probability reflects how exposed D is, not how likely we survive.

label: Daily frequency compounds into habit/retention (the retention advantage)
kill_criterion: Daily use produces daily wrong-answers that erode trust faster than habit forms (H2), OR users automate it away and forget it exists (no felt value).
test_that_resolves_it: Longitudinal use study; track trust/NPS against error rate over 8-12 weeks of daily runs.
evidence: [A - the retention advantage]. CS:LOW. Frequency is a double-edged sword: it's the retention thesis AND the trust-erosion and blast-radius multiplier.

label: Integration depth is the buying criterion and we can meet it
kill_criterion: Buyers require deeper RMM/PSA integration than day-1 ships (ConnectWise-only, ticket-scope permissions), so 'deep integration' buyers won't adopt.
test_that_resolves_it: Confirm required integration depth with Derek-type buyers; audit day-1 scope vs that bar.
evidence: [R] CS:HIGH the criterion is real (Derek: 'only if deep integration into my RMM'). Meeting it day-1 is [A] - build is ConnectWise-only, PSA-scope only.

label: Triage converts MSPs into buyers of A / the platform (the on-ramp, the day-1 reason)
kill_criterion: Triage users do not trial or buy A at a rate that justifies leading go-live with the #6-ranked feature; D remains a standalone commodity with no independent TAM.
test_that_resolves_it: Instrument the funnel: add conversion events to the existing build (triage-user -> A trial -> A purchase); run a cohort and measure lift vs non-triage entry.
evidence: [A - the strategic reason it's day-1]. CS:LOW. ZERO conversion instrumentation in the spec today (FSN-82692 tracks time/completion/success only); other coworkers merely 'bookmarked' (H4).

label: WTP supports the price (Derek max ~$300/mo flat)
kill_criterion: MSPs won't pay a separate/meaningful price for triage because it's table-stakes and self-buildable; ceiling is flat, low, per-tech.
test_that_resolves_it: Van Westendorp / Gabor-Granger on the target segment, isolating triage value from platform value.
evidence: [MEDIUM, single-source] - Derek 'max ~$300/mo flat'. D has no independent TAM; carries A's per-tech TAM, so D double-taxes the same seat.

label: Safe auto-executed diagnostics don't create a blast-radius/liability incident
kill_criterion: An auto-executed low-risk action mis-routes/mis-acts at daily machine scale against a live client PSA, producing a customer-impacting incident.
test_that_resolves_it: Staged rollout with kill-switch and per-action audit; measure auto-action error rate at scale before widening auto-execute scope.
evidence: [A] - NEW HOLE. CS:LOW. Low-risk auto-executes with no human in loop by design (FSN-82692:203); daily frequency multiplies blast radius; unmodeled.

label: False-diagnosis trust erosion stays below the abandonment threshold
kill_criterion: Wrong diagnoses (which the junior tech starts from) accumulate daily and cross the trust-abandonment threshold faster than habit forms.
test_that_resolves_it: Measure diagnosis accuracy on real tickets; correlate error events with abandonment in a longitudinal cohort.
evidence: [A] - NEW HOLE. CS:LOW. Asymmetric and frequency-weighted: a wrong start-point is worse than no start-point, and it happens daily not quarterly.

label: Leading go-live with the #6 feature does NOT poison the #1 (QBR) demand
kill_criterion: First impression 'a router I could build myself' anchors buyer perception/price of the whole platform at commodity level, damaging the premium QBR story.
test_that_resolves_it: Message-order test: does leading with triage vs leading with QBR change perceived platform value / WTP?
evidence: [A] - NEW HOLE. CS:LOW. Offering doc names the sequencing bet (lead with #6, QBR #1 has no spec) but never tests the anchoring cost.

label: ConnectWise-only launch is acceptable coverage AND the PSA dependency is safe
kill_criterion: Autotask/Halo MSPs can't onboard day-1 (coverage cap) OR ConnectWise throttles/reprices/deprecates the API D's core loop depends on.
test_that_resolves_it: Confirm addressable share on ConnectWise vs Autotask/Halo; review ConnectWise API ToS and rate limits for the read/write scopes D needs.
evidence: [VERIFIED] single-PSA fact (FSN-82692:175,251). [A] for dependency risk - D's core read/write loop lives inside a third party's API.

label: 'Live diagnostics' is achievable within permissions MSPs grant a day-1 tool
kill_criterion: Real live diagnostics need RMM/endpoint write-access MSPs won't grant a day-1 tool, so the wedge is not installable until trust is already earned (chicken-and-egg).
test_that_resolves_it: Ask 5-8 MSPs what read/write access they'd grant a brand-new tool day-1; map against the access diagnostics actually require.
evidence: [A] - NEW HOLE. CS:LOW. Day-1 scope is ticket read/write + queue/member read (FSN-82692:316) - enough to route, not to diagnose live.

label: Junior-tech deskilling does not become a retention-inverting cost
kill_criterion: Over 12-18 months juniors lose diagnostic skill because they start from the tool's answer, creating a bench-capability gap the MSP blames on the tool.
test_that_resolves_it: Longitudinal skills tracking in adopting MSPs; qualitative check on whether MSPs perceive deskilling as a risk.
evidence: [A] - NEW HOLE. CS:LOW. Low probability of killing D, named as a second-order retention inversion of the core benefit.

label: The 8.3 intensity signal is independent, not the same 8 people twice
kill_criterion: The intensity (8.3) and qual rank both draw on the same 8-person base; the only independent instrument (n=39) demotes D to #6.
test_that_resolves_it: Rerun intensity on an independent sample disjoint from the original 8; compare to the n=39 forced-rank.
evidence: [D] CS:HIGH on the base-overlap fact (offerings ranking). Small-n qual is directional not projectable - Beth's own triangulation rule.
